official.deadline_note: Applications opened 01:01 NZST on Monday 1 June 2026 and closed 23:50 NZST on Tuesday 4 August 2026 for the 2027-entry round; the separate reference deadline was 23:50 NZST on Friday 7 August 2026, three days after the application deadline. Rhodes House now states applications are closed and will reopen in 2027 for entry to Oxford in 2028, and the next New Zealand constituency dates have not yet been published.
official.application_cycle: 2027-entry round (applications June-August 2026, entry October 2027); applications reopen in 2027 for entry to Oxford in 2028
official.status_note: The Rhodes House applications page states: 'Applications for the Rhodes Scholarship are now closed.' Candidates can join the Rhodes mailing list to be notified when applications reopen in 2027 for entry to the University of Oxford in 2028. For the round just completed, decisions were made in November 2026, with final interviews held in Wellington on 11-12 November 2026.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Universities New Zealand states that Oxford University fees are paid directly by the Rhodes Trust to the College and University; the Rhodes Trust FAQ confirms the Scholarship 'covers Oxford University course fees'.
benefits: Oxford University course fees, paid directly by the Rhodes Trust to the College and University
An annual stipend of £21,060 for the 2026-27 academic year, paid in monthly instalments of £1,755, from which Scholars pay all living expenses including accommodation
Two economy class flights to and from the UK, for the beginning and end of studies in Oxford
The fee required to apply to study at the University of Oxford
Fees for a student visa and the associated International Health Surcharge (IHS), which enables international students to access the UK's National Health Service
A settling in allowance on arrival in Oxford, plus the second visa fee and IHS charges for Scholars who transition to a second course of study in Oxford
eligibility: On 1 August in the year of application, hold New Zealand citizenship or hold a New Zealand Permanent Resident Visa
On 1 August in the year of application, have spent at least five of the previous 10 years in New Zealand

Aged 18-24 on 1 October 2026 (born after 1 October 2001 and on or before 2 October 2008), OR under 27 on 1 October 2026 (born after 1 October 1999) and having completed the first undergraduate degree on or after 1 October 2025

Completed, or expect to complete by July 2027, an undergraduate degree with First-Class Honours or a Master's degree with First-Class Honours, or equivalent, unless an exemption applies because your institution does not offer Honours
Applications from refugees/asylum seekers currently residing in New Zealand will also be considered in this constituency
Meet or exceed the specific entry requirements of the chosen course at the University of Oxford
requirements: Complete and submit the online Rhodes application form before 23:50 NZST on 4 August 2026; there is no application fee and no other form of application is accepted
Nominate six referees - three academic referees who have formally taught and graded you, and three character referees - and register them early in the application form
Ensure referees submit their references online before 23:50 NZST on 7 August 2026
All documents must be submitted in English, with official English translations uploaded where originals are not in English
CV must not exceed two A4 pages at 12pt font and must not include a photograph
Declare that the application is wholly accurate and a fair representation of your achievements, which will be checked for embellishments and inaccuracies
documents: Copy of your birth certificate, or the relevant page of your passport, to prove date of birth and nationality (plus another document showing date of birth if the first does not)

An official transcript showing grades achieved to date - for New Zealand university students this is requested directly from the university; for overseas students and graduates it is your responsibility to obtain your academic record

A full CV covering academic qualifications, publications, prizes, scholarships, positions of leadership, employment, and involvement in student, voluntary, community or political activities, plus cultural, musical or sporting accomplishments (maximum two A4 pages at 12pt, no photograph)
A head-and-shoulders colour photograph in jpg format
A personal statement of no more than 1000 words
An Academic Statement of Study of maximum 450 words presenting a coherent academic plan for the full two years
selection_criteria: Energy to use one's talents to the full, as demonstrated by mastery in areas such as sports, music, debate, dance, theatre and artistic pursuits, particularly where teamwork is involved
Truth, courage, devotion to duty, sympathy for and protection of the weak, kindliness, unselfishness and fellowship
Moral force of character and instincts to lead, and to take an interest in one's fellow beings

Selection is made without regard to financial means, and without regard to marital status, race, ethnic origin, colour, gender, religion, sexual orientation, social background, disability, caste or other irrelevant distinction
coverage: Oxford University course fees, paid directly by the Rhodes Trust to the College and University
An annual stipend from which Scholars pay all living expenses, including accommodation
Two economy class flights to and from the UK
The Oxford application fee, student visa fee and International Health Surcharge
A settling in allowance on arrival in Oxford
application_method: Rhodes House online application system, applying through the New Zealand constituency after using the Rhodes House eligibility checker

Apply to the Rhodes Scholarship before applying to the University of Oxford; selected candidates then apply for their chosen course via the University of Oxford's graduate application form, with support from the team at Rhodes House
Register referees on the referees page of the application form; referees receive an automated email with a unique link to the online reference form
official.application_route: Apply online through the Rhodes House application system via the New Zealand constituency after checking eligibility with the Rhodes House eligibility checker, and before the published closing date.
official.study_mode: Full-time only - the Rhodes Trust states the Scholarship covers full-time courses only and it is not possible to be enrolled in a part-time course while funded
official.citizenship_residency: New Zealand citizenship or a New Zealand Permanent Resident Visa held on 1 August in the year of application, plus at least five of the previous ten years spent living in New Zealand (the criteria require actually living in New Zealand, not merely being technically resident for IRD or similar purposes)
official.international_eligibility: Not open to general international applicants. Eligibility is tied to the New Zealand constituency, which requires New Zealand citizenship or a New Zealand Permanent Resident Visa on 1 August in the year of application; the award is for study at the University of Oxford in the United Kingdom.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: No subject restriction - most full-time postgraduate courses at Oxford are covered. The Rhodes Trust does not cover PGCert or PGDip courses (including the PGCE), the Doctorate of Clinical Psychology (DClinPsych), or the graduate-entry/accelerated degree in Medicine, and the MBA, MPP and MFE are available as a one-year tenure only.
official.research_requirement: For MPhil or DPhil candidates, the Academic Statement of Study must briefly outline the proposed research area, the department in which you propose to work, and one or more Oxford academics you would like to work with.
official.duration: Standard two-year tenure (a two-year scholarship); doctoral study is supported for up to three years of University tuition fees and stipend, and up to four years on the 1+3 pathway
official.description: The Rhodes Scholarship for New Zealand is a partnership between the Rhodes Trust and the Robertson Foundation, administered in New Zealand by Universities New Zealand - Te Pokai Tara. It is a fully funded, full-time postgraduate award supporting outstanding all-round students to study at the University of Oxford in the United Kingdom, with up to three Scholars elected from New Zealand each year.
official.region: New Zealand constituency (Oceania), for study at the University of Oxford, United Kingdom
official.program_type: International postgraduate scholarship, provided by the Rhodes Trust in partnership with the Robertson Foundation and the Second Century Founder John McCall McBain
official.english_requirement: If English is not your first language, you must check that you meet the University of Oxford's English language proficiency requirements at the higher level. No separate Rhodes test score is published for New Zealand applicants.

applicant_utility.summary: This is the Rhodes Trust's own award for New Zealand-connected candidates, worth around £21,060 a year in stipend plus full Oxford fees, two economy flights and visa/health-surcharge costs. The 2027-entry round closed on 4 August 2026, so the realistic target is the round that reopens in 2027 for Oxford entry in October 2028 - use the gap to line up six referees and draft both statements now. Treat the reference deadline (three days after the application deadline) as the real cut-off, because a late reference cannot be rescued.
applicant_utility.best_fit: A New Zealand citizen or Permanent Resident Visa holder aged 18-24 who has just finished or is finishing a First-Class Honours degree and can point to sustained achievement outside the classroom as well as inside it.
application_readiness_checklist: Run the Rhodes House eligibility checker for the New Zealand constituency and confirm your birth date falls inside the published window before investing time in statements

Ask each of your eight New Zealand universities' Rhodes Scholarship Advisers (listed on the Universities New Zealand page) for feedback on your draft, and email scholarships@universitiesnz.ac.nz with any eligibility question

Line up three academic referees who have actually taught and graded you and three character referees for service, sport, music or leadership, and give them the Rhodes Guidance for Referees document rather than a generic request
Ask your university registrar now for the official transcript, since New Zealand transcripts are pulled directly from the university and are outside your control

Draft the 1000-word personal statement against the three published guiding questions, and a separate 450-word Academic Statement of Study that justifies a coherent two-year Oxford plan with a strong second course choice

Check the Oxford course pages for the graduate deadlines that fall in early December (MPP, MSc Global Governance and Diplomacy, MSt Women's Gender and Sexuality Studies, Medical Sciences, and research degrees in Computer Science/Engineering) so your course choices match a viable timetable
common_rejection_risks: Referees missing the 7 August 2026 reference deadline: six references are mandatory and the Trust will not chase them for you, so unregistered or slow referees sink otherwise strong files

Falling outside the immovable age window, or mis-reading the 'first degree' definition - an intercalated honours year inside another degree (for example BHSc(Hons) within MBChB) does not count as a first degree
The five-of-ten-years residency test being judged case by case by the National Secretary, who may demand evidence of time actually spent living in New Zealand rather than IRD technical residency
Claiming First-Class Honours equivalence when your institution does not offer Honours without documenting the exemption grounds in the application
Submitting a course plan with no rationale: selectors explicitly judge how your choices connect to your education and aspirations, and two course applications are expected
Overstating achievements - details are checked for embellishment and inaccuracies, and suspected misrepresentation can get an offer rescinded after selection
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The stipend is sized for one person and the Rhodes Trust takes no financial responsibility for a partner or dependants, so family costs are entirely on you. Travel to New Zealand for the in-person final interview is at your own expense if you are based overseas. A DPhil typically runs 3-4 years while Rhodes fee and stipend liability stops at three years, so you must plan funding for any fourth year, and anything past standard tenure (including second-course costs) needs other sources. Any secondary award worth more than 33% of the stipend (over £6,950 a year) must also be declared.
document_audit: Upload the birth certificate or the passport page that proves both date of birth and nationality - if that document does not show your date of birth you must add a second document that does
Do not put a photograph in your CV, and keep it to two A4 pages at 12pt; the head-and-shoulders colour jpg is a separate upload
Every document must be in English, so budget time and cost for certified translations of non-English transcripts, birth certificates and passports
Do not upload extra certificates, testimonials or links: the Trust explicitly asks you not to submit anything beyond the listed documents
Reference letters must be headed, signed, in English, in PDF format and within two A4 or letter pages, and they must come from institutional or professional email addresses so they can be verified
Referees should not normally be personal friends, peers or relatives; if one is, they must disclose the connection inside the reference
alerts: Applications for the current round are closed; the next window opens in 2027 for Oxford entry in October 2028, and the New Zealand dates are not published yet - sign up for the Rhodes mailing list rather than assuming the same June-August timing

Finalists must attend the final interview and the social engagement in person with no accommodation on date, time or mode - for the 2027 round these were in Wellington on 11-12 November 2026, and overseas candidates funded their own travel

Apply to Rhodes before applying to Oxford: winning the Scholarship is confirmed only upon successful Oxford admission, and the Scholarship cannot be brought forward or deferred to another academic year
You may apply to Rhodes at most twice in total, and only through the same constituency, so a rushed first attempt burns one of your two chances
You cannot hold another substantial scholarship alongside a Rhodes Scholarship, though a smaller secondary award above 33% of the stipend is permitted if declared
The stipend does not cover partners or dependants, and current UK policy limits which students can bring dependants, so check your course type before making family plans
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Submit the online Rhodes House form before the closing date with documents, CV, photo and both statements uploaded, then register six referees who submit their online references three days later; the Trust checks applications for eligibility and completeness, compiles a longlist, prioritises it through a panel review, interviews shortlisted candidates by video, and finishes with an in-person final interview and social engagement before selections are made in November - after which successful candidates apply directly to Oxford with support from Rhodes House.
